title: a repository git refuses to read is taken for no repository by five readers, and vendoring from such a checkout writes "not a git checkout" into the consumer's manifest beside "source: checkout"
body:
## Problem

0179 taught a gate's ignore file to tell a repository git refuses to read (one owned by another user, unless `safe.directory` names it) from no repository, by looking on the filesystem for a `.git` at the root or above it (`git_marker_above`). Five other readers still take a failed git call for no repository. critic-shell found them reviewing 0179, and cc located each one, at the lines main carries once 0179 and 0178 land:

1. `git_head_watch_paths` (lib/helpers:2504): a failure gives no watch paths.
2. `commit_direction` (lib/helpers:3320): it prints `unknown`.
3. `tree_dirty_paths` (lib/install:314): it returns 2, "cannot tell", and its two callers, which publish an install (lib/cmd/install:244, lib/cmd/upgrade:103), refuse with "<source> is not a git repository".
4. `source_commit_of` (lib/install:810): it prints "not a git checkout -- these bytes name no commit", and `manifest_write` writes that line into the consumer's manifest (lib/install:998).
5. `_fullcycle_header` (lib/cmd/fullcycle:469): its else branch prints "dirty: not a checkout -- these bytes are not compared to anything".

fleet's `seam_committed` (bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet:631) already tells the two apart, by git's words under `LC_ALL=C` and a `.git` at the root. The release pre-flight's refusal (lib/cmd/release:579), reached through `gate_out_ignored`, gives "add tmp/ to .gitignore" as its remedy, but a cut or a dry run in a repository git refuses to read never reaches it: step 1, resolve, stops first, where `release_versions` cannot list the tags, in git's own "detected dubious ownership" words (cc measured a cut and a dry run; vc drove the dry run, rc 1, no gate run). When filed, this paragraph said the pre-flight gives that remedy in such a repository, and the Fix and Done when 3 asked for the remedy to change there; release is out of this issue's scope.

Only the fourth writes. Vendoring has no dirty gate, which guards only the publishing of an install, so a project vendored from a devbin checkout that git refuses to read gets a tracked manifest that contradicts itself.

## Measured (vc, 2026-10-07, main 72f92d7c, git 2.56.0)

A clone of devbin as the source, and `bin/devbin install --into <proj> --name demo` run from it with `GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1`, git's switch for a repository owned by another user (git: "fatal: detected dubious ownership"). The run exits 0 with 74 files vendored, and the manifest reads `# source: checkout` above `# source_commit: not a git checkout -- these bytes name no commit`. The same command without the variable records `# source_commit: 72f92d7c9beeec737700e38a866c50a9cfe57cbd`. Scratch: ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-vc/0.1.10/refused/.

## Fix

One reading of a failed git call, shared by every reader: no `.git` at the root or above it (`git_marker_above`'s plain no) is no repository, and a `.git` there is a repository git would not answer for. Each reader says which in its own words. `source_commit_of` writes eg "a checkout git could not read -- these bytes name no commit". The publish refusal says git could not read the source, with git's own first line, not that it is no repository. "Could not read" rather than "refused": the filesystem reading cannot tell git's refusal from a checkout with no git on PATH or a `.git` git passes over, and "could not read" stays true of each. fullcycle's header does the same. release is unchanged, and an arm holds that a cut in such a repository stops at step 1 in git's words, before the pre-flight. `seam_committed` moves onto the shared reading, which is read from the filesystem rather than from git's words. The first two readers keep their answers, no watch paths and `unknown`, which are right either way, and a comment says so.

## Done when

1. Vendoring from a checkout git refuses to read writes a `source_commit` line saying that git could not read it, never "not a git checkout"; the arm is driven with `GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1` and is red on main first.
2. Publishing from such a checkout refuses in words that say git could not read it, with git's own first line.
3. fullcycle's header says the same of a repository git refuses to read, and `seam_committed` answers through the shared reading. A cut in such a repository still stops at step 1 in git's own words, before the pre-flight, held by an arm.

When filed, the Fix and Done when 1 and 2 said git "refused" the checkout. They say "could not read" since critic-shell's review of 0185 (cc, 2026-10-07), for the reason the Fix gives.

## Resolution

Landed at 9e640723 on a green full suite (vc's, 2243 of 2243 ok, 0 not ok, .errors empty, seal 20261008-0655). A failed git call is read once, by git_repo_absent in lib/helpers: no repository only when no `.git` sits at the directory or above it, as far up as git's own discovery looks, which honours GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES as git reads it, with the directory spelled as git spells it; anything else is a checkout git could not read. Vendoring from a checkout git refuses records `a checkout git could not read -- these bytes name no commit` beside `source: checkout`, never "not a git checkout" (Done when 1; "could not read" says that of a refusal and stays true of the other cases the reading cannot call absent). The publish refusal, now one publish_gate for install and upgrade, names a repository git cannot read and carries git's own first line, "detected dubious ownership" for another user's (Done when 2), and a corrupt index's own reason. fullcycle's header says "dirty: a checkout git could not read", and its probe no longer follows an inherited GIT_DIR. fleet's census answers through the shared reading: no repository is `not a checkout`, a `.git` of the estate's own that git cannot read, or a root that cannot be entered, is UNREADABLE and fails the scan, and a `.git` only above it is `not its own checkout`. A cut and a dry run in a refused repository stop at step 1 in git's own words, before the pre-flight, held by an arm (Done when 3); release is unchanged. lib/runlog's gate asks the same reading in place of its own copy. Held by 24 arms, among them an oracle that asks git and the reading the same question over 17 ceiling forms, and five case spellings on a disk that folds case; 16 are red on the base, and the other eight are 0179's, AT-1.4 and guards. 34 mutants, 34 killed. A failed call in a repository whose index git cannot read, where --version prints a bare commit, fullcycle's header exits 128, check's builtin critic says nothing is staged and the release pre-flight offers its remedy, is 0186's.
